expected_behavior: tick() must measure elapsed time as the CURRENT time minus holdStartTime, not a value captured once when the button was constructed. Holding for less than holdDurationMs must not fire; reaching or exceeding holdDurationMs while still holding must fire the completion effect exactly once; continuing to hold afterward must not fire it again; releasing before the threshold must not fire it at all; a fresh hold attempt after an early release must still be able to succeed normally.
allowed_repairs: call clock.now() fresh inside tick() (e.g. `const elapsed = clock.now() - state.holdStartTime;`) instead of reusing a value captured once at construction time
forbidden_repairs: firing on pointerdown immediately, skipping the duration check entirely -- caught by holding_less_than_threshold_does_not_fire and early_release_does_not_fire, both of which pass on the original buggy fixture (vacuously, since nothing ever fires) and must continue to pass after a correct fix
removing the holding/tick state machine and replacing it with an unconditional always-armed confirm
changing holdDurationMs's default or the public shape of createHoldButton's return value beyond what's needed for the fix
